decision.summary: Tenant says the landlord's LG washer has failed and offers to replace it with their own machine. That needs landlord consent, so I asked the landlord for consent and for decisions on the old machine and on who pays removal and fitting. I told the tenant and put the job on hold until 2025-07-30.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: At intake, routine. It is not a plain repair: the tenant proposes replacing the landlord's washer with their own. Landlord consent and the disposal of the old LG and costs are outstanding.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Landlord approval request sent via the agency landlord record (A1). Tenant updated by email (A2). Hold until 2025-07-30 (A4).

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: No human escalation. The decision belongs to the landlord, who has been asked. Escalate only if the landlord stays silent after the chase.

assumptions: The washer is landlord-owned because it was there at move-in, per the tenant; not verified against the inventory

args.decision_needed: The tenant reports the landlord's LG washing machine (there when they moved in) has failed with a power fault and says it can't be fixed (their own web research, not confirmed by an engineer). They offer to buy a replacement themselves, which would remain their property and be taken with them when they leave. Please tell us: (1) do you consent to the tenant installing their own machine; (2) what should happen to the existing LG (inspect/repair, dispose, or keep); (3) who pays to disconnect and remove the old machine and fit the new one; or (4) whether you would rather we send our contractor to inspect/repair it, or arrange your own.
options: Consent to tenant's own machine; state who pays for removal of the old one and fitting, and what happens to the old LG
Our contractor inspects the LG first and quotes repair or replacement
You arrange your own contractor or replacement

args.body: Thanks for letting us know about the washing machine. Fitting your own machine needs the landlord's consent, so we've put your offer to them, including that it would stay yours and go with you if you move. We've also asked what should happen to the current LG and who covers removing it and fitting the new one. Please don't disconnect or remove the old machine until we confirm. If you can, send a photo of the machine and any error code. We'll update you by 2025-07-30 at the latest.
